name: radio_listen
description:
Returns the subscriptions (`subscription_id`, `subscription_url`) holding received messages that no query has read yet. With `wait_for_messages = true` and nothing unread, it blocks until a message arrives or `timeout` passes, then returns whatever is unread (possibly no rows). Reading messages with `radio_received_messages` or `radio_subscription_received_messages` marks them seen, so the next `radio_listen` waits for new ones.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** a message that arrives while `radio_listen` is checking the subscriptions now wakes it immediately (previously it could be missed and the call slept for the full timeout), concurrent listeners no longer cancel each other's wake-ups, the wait continues until the timeout instead of sometimes returning early with no rows, and the wait can be interrupted (Ctrl-C).

examples.description: Wait up to 10 seconds for unread messages on any subscription

examples.code: SELECT subscription_url FROM radio_listen(false, INTERVAL '0 seconds');
examples.skip: DuckDB 2.0 build only (loopback transport / new columns); not available in Haybarn 1.5

name: radio_subscribe
description:
Opens a subscription and returns its `subscription_id`. The URL is the subscription's key for every other `radio_*` function; subscribing to a URL that is already subscribed returns the existing id. Supported URLs: `ws://` / `wss://` (WebSocket), `redis://host:port?channel=name` (Redis Pub/Sub; `redis-tcp://`, `redis-tls://` and `redis-unix://` are also accepted). The connection is made in the background. Optional named parameters: `receive_message_capacity` (default 1000; the oldest message is dropped when the receive queue is full), `transmit_retry_initial_delay_ms` (default 100), `transmit_retry_multiplier` (default 1.5, must be > 1) and `transmit_retry_max_delay_ms` (default 10000).

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** refuses network URLs when `enable_external_access` is false (Permission Error). Adds a `loopback://name` transport that needs no server: messages transmitted on it are received by the same subscription, and it works with external access disabled. A prepared `radio_subscribe` returns its row on every `EXECUTE`.

examples.description: Subscribe to a Redis channel with a larger receive queue
A loopback subscription for testing, no server needed (DuckDB 2.0)
examples.skip: DuckDB 2.0 build only (loopback transport / new columns); not available in Haybarn 1.5

name: radio_unsubscribe
description: Closes the subscription for a URL and returns its `subscription_id`. Its received messages and queued transmit messages are discarded. Raises an error if the URL is not subscribed.

examples.skip: DuckDB 2.0 build only (loopback transport / new columns); not available in Haybarn 1.5

name: radio_subscriptions
description:
Lists the active subscriptions: `subscription_id`, `url`, `creation_time`, `activation_time` (NULL until connected), `disabled`, `received_last_message_time`, `received_messages_processed`, `transmit_messages_processed`, `transmit_last_queue_time`, `transmit_last_success_time`, `transmit_last_failure_time`, `transmit_successes` and `transmit_failures`.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** adds `received_messages_queued` (messages currently in the receive queue) and `received_messages_dropped_unseen` (messages evicted from a full receive queue before any query read them — raise `receive_message_capacity` or read more often if this grows).

examples.code: SELECT url, received_messages_queued, received_messages_dropped_unseen FROM radio_subscriptions();
examples.skip: DuckDB 2.0 build only (loopback transport / new columns); not available in Haybarn 1.5

name: radio_received_messages
description:
Returns the messages held in every subscription's receive queue: `subscription_id`, `subscription_url`, `message_id`, `message_type` (`message`, `error`, `connection`, `disconnection`), `receive_time`, `seen_count`, `channel` and the `message` payload as `BLOB` (use `decode(message)` for UTF-8 text). Reading a message increments its `seen_count`; messages stay in the queue until they are evicted by newer ones or the subscription is closed.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** the queue is read when the query runs, so a prepared statement sees current messages on every `EXECUTE`.

examples.code: SELECT receive_time, channel, decode(message) AS text FROM radio_received_messages() WHERE message_type = 'message' ORDER BY receive_time DESC LIMIT 100;

examples.description: Messages injected into a loopback subscription (DuckDB 2.0)
examples.code: SELECT channel, decode(message) AS text, seen_count FROM radio_received_messages();
examples.skip: DuckDB 2.0 build only (loopback transport / new columns); not available in Haybarn 1.5

name: radio_subscription_received_messages
description: Returns the messages in one subscription's receive queue: `message_id`, `receive_time`, `seen_count`, `channel` and `message` (`BLOB`). Reading increments `seen_count`. Raises an error if the URL is not subscribed.

examples.code: SELECT receive_time, decode(message) AS text FROM radio_subscription_received_messages('wss://stream.example.com/events') ORDER BY receive_time DESC;
SELECT message_id, decode(message) AS text FROM radio_subscription_received_messages('loopback://demo');
examples.skip: DuckDB 2.0 build only (loopback transport / new columns); not available in Haybarn 1.5

name: radio_subscription_received_message_add
description:
Adds a message to a subscription's receive queue as if it had arrived from the network and returns its `message_id`. Useful for testing SQL that consumes `radio_*` tables without a real upstream. Wakes any waiting `radio_listen`.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** the message may be `VARCHAR` (previously only `BLOB`, so non-ASCII text had to be cast) and the channel may be `NULL`.

examples.description: Inject a test message (DuckDB 2.0: loopback transport)
examples.skip: DuckDB 2.0 build only (loopback transport / new columns); not available in Haybarn 1.5

name: radio_transmit_message
description:
Queues `message` for sending on the subscription for `url` and returns its `message_id`. A background sender delivers it, retrying with exponential backoff (see the `radio_subscribe` retry parameters) until it is sent, `max_attempts` attempts fail, or `expire_duration` passes. A `VARCHAR` payload is sent as a WebSocket text frame and a `BLOB` payload as a binary frame; for Redis the message is `PUBLISH`ed to `channel` (required for Redis, ignored for WebSocket). A NULL message is an error. Track delivery with `radio_subscription_transmit_messages` and wait for it with `radio_flush`.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** refuses network subscriptions when `enable_external_access` is false (Permission Error). On a `loopback://` subscription the message is delivered to the subscription's own receive queue.

examples.description: Round trip on a loopback subscription (DuckDB 2.0)
examples.skip: DuckDB 2.0 build only (loopback transport / new columns); not available in Haybarn 1.5

name: radio_subscription_transmit_messages
description: Returns one subscription's transmit queue: `message_id`, `creation_time`, `last_attempt_start_time`, `last_attempt_end_time`, `state` (`pending`, `sending`, `sent`, `retries_exhausted`, `time_expired`), `expire_duration_ms`, `max_attempts`, `try_count`, `channel`, `message` and `result` (the last transport error, if any). Finished messages stay until removed with `radio_subscription_transmit_messages_delete_finished`.

examples.code: SELECT message_id, state, try_count, result FROM radio_subscription_transmit_messages('wss://stream.example.com/events') ORDER BY message_id DESC;

examples.description: After sending on a loopback subscription (DuckDB 2.0)
examples.skip: DuckDB 2.0 build only (loopback transport / new columns); not available in Haybarn 1.5

name: radio_subscription_transmit_message_delete
description: Removes one message, by `message_id`, from a subscription's transmit queue, cancelling it if it has not been sent yet. Returns true.

examples.description: Cancel a queued message (DuckDB 2.0: loopback transport)
examples.skip: DuckDB 2.0 build only (loopback transport / new columns); not available in Haybarn 1.5

name: radio_subscription_transmit_messages_delete_finished
description: Removes the transmit messages of a subscription that are finished — `sent`, `retries_exhausted` or `time_expired` — and returns true. Pending messages are kept.

examples.description: Clean up the outbox (DuckDB 2.0: loopback transport)
examples.skip: DuckDB 2.0 build only (loopback transport / new columns); not available in Haybarn 1.5

name: radio_flush
description:
Waits up to `timeout` for every subscription's transmit queue to finish (send, or give up on) its pending messages. Returns `all_messages_flushed`: true if everything finished in time, false otherwise. It does not touch received messages.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** the wait can be interrupted, and a prepared `radio_flush` checks the current subscriptions on every `EXECUTE`.

examples.description: Wait up to 5 seconds for outgoing messages

name: radio_sleep
description:
Sleeps for `duration` and returns true. A convenience for scripts that poll between reads.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** the sleep can be interrupted and a negative duration is an error.

name: radio_version
description:
Returns the version of the loaded Radio extension.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** returns the build version (`YYYYMMDDNN`, e.g. `2026110701`), the same value the extension reports elsewhere; it previously returned a stale `20250601.02`.
